newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Heineken to take stake in Tempo.
newsitem.headline: Heineken to take stake in Tempo.

text.p: Heineken NV -- Europe's biggest brewer -- said on Monday it had signed a letter of intent on the purchase of a stake of at least 51 percent in Israeli company Tempo Beer Industries.
"We have signed a letter of intent, which is the basis for further negotiations," spokeswoman Margritha Meijer said.
She said the letter of intent included the possibility of splitting Tempo into separate beer and soft drinks companies but added that no final decision had been made on this.
Tempo currently imports and sells the Dutch company's Heineken and Amstel beer brands in Israel.
The letter of intent follows a 90-day purchase option granted to Heineken on February 3, Meijer said.
Israel's Bar-Bornstein group, which already holds 51 percent of Tempo, agreed on February 3 to acquire a 44.5 percent stake controlled by the rival Podhorzer group for $42 million.
Tempo said at the time that its controlling shareholders had reached an agreement aimed at making Heineken a strategic partner and shareholder.

"On March 13, 1997 a letter of intent was signed by the Heineken group and the Bar-Bornstein group concerning the readiness of Heineken to acquire more than 51 percent of the issued share capital of Tempo Beer Industries," Tempo said in a statement to the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) on March 13.
